name: Pagan Kingdom
native: ပုဂံပြည် (Băgam pyi)

predecessors.name: Pyu city-states
predecessors.text: the Pyu cities of the Irrawaddy dry zone: Pagan's own land from 849 and the rest of the Pyu realm (Sri Ksetra, the Mu valley) by the mid-11th century

predecessors.name: Mon city-states
predecessors.text: Thaton and the Mon country of Lower Burma, taken in 1057

successors.name: Myinsaing Kingdom
successors.text: the small area around the capital that Kyawswa controlled from 1289: the heartland principality of about 320 by 130 km

successors.name: Hanthawaddy Kingdom
successors.text: Ramannadesa, which Wareru declared independent on 30 January 1287

successors.name: Yuan dynasty
successors.text: northern Burma to Tagaung, which the Mongols held as the province of Zhengmian (the gazetteer has no name for it)

successors.name: Shan States
successors.text: the Shan Hills, which broke away in 1287

ledger.x: 849: Pyinbya founds Pagan on the Irrawaddy.
860: the principality grows in Cliopatria's staging (5,400 to 26,800 km2).
960: the Burmans lead the dry zone in Cliopatria's staging (26,800 to 44,600 km2).
1044: Anawrahta comes to power at Pagan and the Pyu remainder passes under Pagan.
1057: the Shan Hills and the northern uplands come under Pagan.
1057: Anawrahta conquers Thaton and Lower Burma.
1066: Pagan reaches the Tenasserim coast, the Chin Hills and the Kayin and Mon uplands.
1283: the Mongol invasion reaches the frontier forts.
1284: northern Burma to Tagaung passes to the Yuan.
1287: Arakan stops paying tribute to Pagan.
1287: the rest of the kingdom dissolves around the capital.

wars.name: Conquest of Thaton
wars.outcome: Anawrahta invaded the south in early 1057 and Pagan forces took Thaton on 17 May 1057; Pegu submitted and was held as a vassal; Lower Burma came under Pagan.

wars.name: Khmer-Pagan clash on the Tenasserim coast
wars.outcome: Khmer forces invaded Tenasserim and Anawrahta's generals repulsed them; the date is not given, so the span is the reign.

wars.name: Revolts of Arakan and Martaban
wars.outcome: Revolts in Macchagiri (Arakan) and Martaban in 1256-1259 under Narathihapate; Martaban rebelled again in 1285; no change of border is recorded.

wars.name: First Mongol invasion of Burma
wars.outcome: Burmese defeat at Ngasaunggyan (Kanngai) in April 1277; the Mongols invaded on 22 September 1283, took Tagaung on 5 February 1284 and held northern Burma to Tagaung as the province of Zhengmian to 1303; the Pagan kingdom collapsed in 1287.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey on the pages opened fixes any Pagan frontier; the Shan Hills, Tenasserim and Arakan edges are approximate (the chronicles' claims to Chiang Mai and Kengtung are not drawn).
